metadata.title: Significant On Tuesday
metadata.audience: anyone who has an A/B test running and a dashboard they can refresh
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Greek, one word. Not reused — prior: Hola/Jambo, Ciao/Hej, Sawubona/Merhaba, Namaste, Bonjour, Annyeong, Olá, Shalom, Vanakkam, Selam, Konnichiwa.
metadata.note: Track ai-. Every number comes from peeking_evidence.py / beat_data.py, both shipped here: 20,000 simulated A/A experiments, seed 20261106, 2,000 visitors per arm, a look every 100. The arms are IDENTICAL by construction, so every 'winner' is a false positive and no effect has to be assumed. Two corrections were made during the build and both are recorded in FACTCHECK.md: the matched-power comparison in §7 (the first pass compared at a fixed horizon, which flatters the naive method) and the winner's-curse histogram range (±8pp silently dropped a sixth of the mass; it is now ±15pp with the remainder clipped, not discarded). New components this reel: ThresholdWalk + ThresholdWalk916, built against a GATE L punt and logged to TEMPLATE-MISSES.md.

beats.narration_text: Yassou. This is Jainil. Somebody starts an A/B test on Monday, checks it on Tuesday, and on Tuesday it is significant. So they ship it. Today, what that habit actually costs — measured across twenty thousand experiments where the two versions were identical by construction, so every winner is a false one.

show.event: serif greeting lands above the composer
the question types itself into the composer
send arms terracotta, running indicator spins
two output lines land

props.command: My A/B test was significant on Tuesday and isn't today. Which reading do I trust?
output: You never counted how many times you looked.

beats.narration_text: Keep checking an A/B test, and you will eventually see noise. Not because the test is broken. Because looking is itself a decision, and nobody ever counted how many times you looked.

show.event: cursor blinks on an empty page
the line types out, ending on the word truth
truth goes terracotta, hesitates, deletes
noise types in its place

props.text:
Keep checking an A/B test
and you will eventually see truth.

qc.reason: Deliberately sparse typographic beat — EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW renders beat 2 as the hesitant writer on an otherwise empty page. Every prior reel waives the fill floor here.

beats.narration_text: Here is one of those twenty thousand. Both versions are identical, so the true difference is exactly zero. After the first hundred visitors per arm it is already outside the line — significant, in favour of B. Stop on Tuesday and you ship B. Keep going and it wanders back. By two thousand visitors there is nothing there, because there was never anything there.

show.event: title, then the terracotta band draws and holds still
the walk starts drawing left to right
the first point sits outside the band and lights terracotta
callout: significant here
the walk settles on the zero line, end callout lands

props.title: ONE A/A TEST, READ TWENTY TIMES
props.caption: Both versions are identical. The true difference is zero at every point on this line.

beats.narration_text: So how often does that happen? Look once, at the end, and five percent of these null experiments come back significant — which is exactly what a five percent test promises. Look twice and it is nearly nine. Five times, fifteen. Twenty times, over twenty-five percent. The test never got worse. You just gave it more chances to be wrong.

show.event: title lands, axis sets
the one-look bar grows to 5.0 as the promise is spoken
bars two and five grow in narration order
the twenty-look bar grows past all of them and takes the accent
caption lands under the plot

props.title: FALSE WINNERS, BY HOW OFTEN YOU LOOK
props.caption: 20,000 experiments where the two arms are identical. Same data, same test, same 5% line.

beats.narration_text: And a wrong call is not the worst of it. This is every difference measured by the runs that did stop early. Remember the truth is zero. There is nothing near zero. Not one of them stopped at under one point eight points, and the middle one said four point four. A small effect is never significant at a small sample — so the only way to stop early is to measure a big one.

show.event: title, then the axis with zero marked at centre
the density fills in — two lobes, nothing between them
the empty middle is marked in terracotta on the spoken nothing near zero
the readout lands: truth 0.00, median measured 4.40

props.title: WHAT THE EARLY STOPPERS MEASURED
props.caption: 5,081 runs that stopped significant. None of them could have reported a small effect.

beats.narration_text: The fix is not to stop looking. It is to move the line. Split your five percent across the looks the Bonferroni way and you land at one point eight — safe, but you have thrown away power you already paid for. Calibrate a single boundary for the number of looks you actually take, and twenty-five percent falls back to five. Same data. Same peeking. One number changed.

show.event: three cards land left to right
the first card's 25.4% reads as the problem
the Bonferroni card lands with its cost noted
the calibrated card takes the accent at 5.1%

props.title: THREE LINES, SAME TWENTY LOOKS
props.caption: Boundary calibrated by simulation on held-out null runs, not fitted to the runs it is scored on.

beats.narration_text: Here is Tuesday again, with the calibrated line. The run that fooled us never reaches it. That is not free — a wider boundary needs a bigger cap, and below about sixty-five percent power you will spend more visitors than one fixed test would. Above it you spend fewer. At eighty percent power, nineteen percent fewer, because a real effect gets called early.

show.event: the same walk returns, but the band is wider
the walk draws — every point now sits inside the band
no point lights terracotta; the callout reads held
caption lands with the cost

props.title: THE SAME TUESDAY, CALIBRATED
props.caption: Costs more visitors below ~65% power. Saves 19% at 80%, where real effects stop it early.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Simulate an A/B test where both arms are identical, check for significance every hundred users, stop at the first p below point oh five, then report how often you declare a winner and how big the effect looked when you did. Run it on your own numbers. The second answer is the one that will bother you, because it tells you what your past wins probably looked like.

show.event: Your turn. lands in the greeting slot
the prompt types into the composer, read aloud as it goes
send arms terracotta and holds

props.segment: Run it on a test you own
props.command: Simulate an A/B test where both arms are identical. Check significance every 100 users and stop at the first p < 0.05. Report how often it declares a winner, and how large the measured effect is when it does.

beats.narration_text: Significant on Tuesday. This is Jainil. Subscribe.
